title: fix(plugin-sharing): scope getRule's by-id branch to the caller's organization
body:
Fixes #7761

## The defect

`SharingRuleService.getRule` resolved an id with a bare `{id: idOrName}` predicate and no organization filter, executed under the service's `SYSTEM_CTX` so nothing re-scoped it downstream. All three verbs resolve through `getRule`, so all three inherited the hole:

- `GET /api/v1/sharing/rules/:id` — read another tenant's rule (criteria, recipient, access level);
- `POST /api/v1/sharing/rules/:id/evaluate` — materialise that tenant's grants on demand;
- `DELETE /api/v1/sharing/rules/:id` — delete the rule **and purge every `sys_record_share` grant it had materialised**, i.e. silently revoke another tenant's record access.

The caller needed `manage_sharing` in their own organization and an opaque `srule_...` id. Neither is a tenant boundary: `manage_sharing` is declared `scope: 'org'` in the spec's capability registry, and ids leak through logs, exports, support tickets and the evaluate endpoint's own `{ruleId}` response.

## The fix

One predicate. The by-id lookup now goes through the same `adminOrgScope` helper #7760 introduced for the by-name path, rather than a second scoping helper:

```ts
where: this.adminOrgScope({ id: idOrName }, orgId),
```

so the read is `id = {id} AND (organization_id = {orgId} OR organization_id IS NULL)` when the caller carries an organization, and unfiltered when it does not. Two behaviours are deliberately preserved:

- **No-org (system / boot) contexts are unchanged** — boot seeding, hooks and backfills keep resolving any row by id.
- **Platform-global (`organization_id = null`) rows stay reachable by id**, for symmetry with the by-name path #7760 shipped.

Reaching another organization's rule by id is now indistinguishable from addressing one that does not exist: `getRule` answers `null` (REST 404), `evaluateRule` throws `RULE_NOT_FOUND`, and `deleteRule` is a no-op leaving the row and its grants intact. `deleteRule` staying a silent no-op is deliberate — it keeps delete idempotent and gives the caller no existence oracle for other tenants' ids.

## Caller audit (verified on this branch, not inherited from #7676)

Every in-repo caller was re-checked rather than taken from the #7676 audit. The only callers passing a non-system context are the three REST routes above (`packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts:9268/9287/9305`), which pass the resolved auth context and are exactly the surface being fixed. Every other caller passes a system context with no organization and so takes the unfiltered branch unchanged:

- `sharing-plugin.ts:86` boot reconcile and `:352` rebind — `{isSystem: true}`;
- `sharing-rule-service.ts` `evaluateAllRulesForObject` — `SYSTEM_CTX`;
- `bulk-recompute.ts` / `rule-hooks.ts` — reach rules through `listRules` / `evaluateAllForRecord`, not `getRule` by id;
- the two dogfood tests that call `evaluateRule` (`showcase-bu-hierarchy-sharing`, `showcase-d3-d4-capabilities`) resolve **by name** under a system context.

No caller depends on by-id reaching an arbitrary organization's row.

## The second axis is NOT decided here

An org admin deleting a **platform-global** row affects every tenant until the next boot reseeds it, and #7760 made those rows discoverable. Whether read/evaluate/delete should split for the null-org case is a maintainer call, not a dev judgment, so this PR does not implement a split — it is filed separately as #7795 and cross-linked from #7761. Note this PR neither introduces nor widens that exposure: after #7760, `deleteRule(name, orgAdmin)` already reaches a platform-global row by name on `main` today.

## Tests

New `[#7761]` block in `sharing-rule.test.ts`, modelled on #7676's hand-built org contexts (the package's unit fakes have no notion of a resolved authenticated context, and `bootStack` cannot mint an org-scoped admin — #7762 — so an HTTP-layer test of this path would be structurally non-discriminating in the open core and none was written).

Both directions are pinned: another organization's rule unreachable by id across read/evaluate/delete; platform-global rows still reachable; the caller's own rows unchanged including a **successful** delete; and a no-org boot context still resolving any row. The delete pin asserts the victim's `sys_record_share` grants survive, not just its rule row — grant purging is the actual harm, and a row-only assertion would pass over a fix that still purged them.

```
Test Files  16 passed (16)
     Tests  436 passed (436)
```

`pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-sharing typecheck` clean; `check:engine-double-contract` OK (150 pinned, 2 exempt — the fake engine is untouched); `check-nul-bytes` OK.

### Ablation, direction predicted in advance

Prediction: restoring `where: { id: idOrName }` turns the three "unreachable by id" tests red while the platform-global, own-org, boot and fixture-integrity pins stay green. Measured, exactly that — 3 failed / 433 passed:

```
FAIL  [#7761] ... another organization's rule is unreachable BY ID — read
        AssertionError: expected { ...(15) } to be null
FAIL  [#7761] ... another organization's rule is unreachable BY ID — evaluate
        AssertionError: promise resolved "{ ...(6) }" instead of rejecting
FAIL  [#7761] ... unreachable BY ID — delete leaves the row AND its grants intact
        AssertionError: expected undefined to be truthy
```

The third is the cross-tenant deletion itself, reproduced live: under the unfixed code the victim's rule row is gone. The whole `[#7676]` block stays green throughout, so this change does not disturb what its predecessor shipped.
